changes_made.explanation: This paper studies backdoor attacks, not NLG evaluation. While it mentions sequence-to-sequence tasks, NLG is used as an attack vector, not as the primary evaluation focus. The paper does not evaluate or propose NLG methods.

The paper mentions ROUGE and Exact Match as metrics used to measure backdoor attack success on the Seq2Seq task, but these are not used for NLG evaluation - they measure how well the poisoned model produces the target output when triggered. This is not evaluating the quality of NLG systems.
No LLMs are used as judges for evaluation in this paper.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about security/attacks in federated learning, not about NLG evaluation. While it uses NLG tasks (text classification and sequence-to-sequence) as attack scenarios, the focus is on demonstrating backdoor vulnerabilities rather than evaluating or improving NLG systems. The metrics mentioned (ROUGE, accuracy) are used to measure attack success, not to evaluate NLG quality. This paper should likely be excluded from an NLG evaluation survey.
